claims.statement: @djimitflo/mcp-server (packages/mcp-server) ships a `djimitflo-mcp` binary that starts an McpServer named 'djimitflo' and registers thirteen tool families, exposing Djimitflo loop, goal, agent, mission-control, orchestration, governance, knowledge, and DjimitSec scan capabilities to MCP clients over stdio or an authenticated HTTP/SSE transport.

Most MCP tools query Djimitflo's SQLite database directly via better-sqlite3 rather than through the REST API; only the council, approval, export, explainer-run, and djimitsec scan-dispatch tools deliberately call the authenticated API.

The entrypoint parses `--transport` (default stdio), `--port` (default 3002), and `--db` (fallback DJIMITFLO_DB), opens the database once with createDatabase, and builds fresh McpServer instances per connection via a createServer factory.

The stdio transport wraps the server connect in runWithMcpAuth with a synthetic principal: sub from DJIMITFLO_MCP_STDIO_PRINCIPAL or `stdio:<uid>`, token from DJIMITFLO_MCP_TOKEN, role hardwired to UserRole.VIEWER with a 24-hour expiry; the viewer role carries only read:evidence and read:repository, so permission-guarded mutating and audit tools fail with MCP_PERMISSION_DENIED for default stdio sessions (gated notebook/explainer writes surface it as an isError result).

The HTTP transport (transports/http.ts) refuses to start without JWT_SECRET and serves the legacy SSE protocol at /mcp (GET opens a session stream, POST delivers messages to the per-session transport), with an unauthenticated /health probe.

Every HTTP request requires a Bearer token verified by verifyHs256Jwt from @djimitflo/shared/jwt, which rejects non-HS256 algorithms, bad signatures (timing-safe compare), unknown roles, missing sub, and expired or not-yet-valid tokens.

On the HTTP transport, currentPrincipal revalidates signed claims against a live authority database: the user must be active with a known role, organization_id must match the stored assignment, and tokens carrying an sid must have a non-revoked, unexpired refresh_tokens row; on success role and email are rebound from the database so revocation and demotion take effect immediately.

With a snapshot or missing authority database the HTTP verifier rejects sid-bearing tokens (a static signature check cannot prove a session family is alive) while sid-less tokens pass on signature; a failing live lookup returns null (refusal) and never falls back to signature-only trust.

Each HTTP MCP session records a principal key of (sub, role, organization_id, sid) at stream setup, and every POST's verified token must produce the same key, returning 403 on mismatch to prevent session reuse by a different or modified principal.

resolveDatabasePath picks the database from --db or DJIMITFLO_DB/DB_PATH (relative paths resolved against INIT_CWD, then cwd), otherwise the first existing candidate among <monorepo>/.data/djimitflo.sqlite, <cwd>/.data/djimitflo.sqlite, and <cwd>/djimitflo.sqlite; startup throws when nothing resolves or the file is missing, and the handle opens with foreign_keys=ON.

The DbHandle mode is 'live' only when DJIMITFLO_DATA_MODE is exactly 'live'; any other value or absence yields the default 'snapshot', and mutating tools call requireLiveMode which throws DJIMITFLO_LIVE_DATA_REQUIRED on snapshot handles.

requireLiveMode additionally requires the database's system_state row database_instance_id (throwing DJIMITFLO_DATABASE_ID_REQUIRED when absent) and throws DJIMITFLO_DATABASE_ID_MISMATCH when DJIMITFLO_EXPECTED_INSTANCE_ID is set and differs, preventing silent mutation of the wrong database.

databaseProvenance reports instance_id (from system_state), node_id (DJIMITFLO_NODE_ID or hostname), resolved path, mode (defaulting to snapshot), and DJIMITFLO_COMMIT_SHA, and is surfaced by mission-control and governance provenance tools.

MCP auth context is stored in AsyncLocalStorage via runWithMcpAuth/currentMcpAuth; currentMcpAuth throws MCP_AUTH_CONTEXT_REQUIRED outside a context, so anonymous tool invocation is impossible regardless of transport.

Write tools mirror the permission of their HTTP route twin by checking the principal's role against ROLE_PERMISSIONS from @djimitflo/shared and throwing MCP_PERMISSION_DENIED: spawn_agent and handoff_agent require write:swarm_action, approve_action requires create:task, authority_emit and mutating notebook tools require write:evidence, authority_trace/authority_stats require read:audit, governance catalog writers require manage:config, explainer_create_task/explainer_run_task require write:governance, and djimitflo_scan_repository requires create:task plus execute:task.

Platform tools (djimitflo_council_ask, djimitflo_generate_export) and orchestration approve_action forward currentMcpAuth().token as a Bearer header to DJIMITFLO_API_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3001/api), so the REST API re-applies its own authorization to those calls.

The loops, goals, agents, and mission-control families are read-only SQL views over loop_runs, worker_leases, loop_events, goals, and agents tables; mission-control and system-health responses always include databaseProvenance.

djimitflo_spawn_agent is registration-only: it inserts an idle agents row with metadata flags registration_only:true and context_budget_enforced:false and never creates tasks, worker leases, context allocations, or executions; handoff_agent writes a pending fleet_handoffs control-plane row; approve_action creates a pending approval via the API without executing the action.

The governance family mixes read-only inspection tools (provenance, doctor, server/tool/permission listings, cost summary, evidence chain, openmythos runs, skill outcomes) with three mutating sync/probe tools (djimitflo_sync_mcp_catalog, djimitflo_sync_http_sidecar_catalog, djimitflo_probe_mcp_sidecars) that default to apply=false dry-run previews and gate writes behind both requireLiveMode and requireMcpPermission('manage:config') — the permission of their HTTP route twins.

Tool-name classification for synced permissions pins djimitflo_scan_repository to requires_approval/medium, assigns requires_approval/high to names matching approve|spawn|handoff, assigns allowed/medium to names matching evidence|cost|permission|mcp_ and allowed/low otherwise, and classifies OpenAPI GET/HEAD/OPTIONS operations as allowed/low while other HTTP methods become requires_approval/medium, so freshly synced permissions start conservative.

djimitflo_authority_emit appends only observational HOLD/DENY events to the authority ledger — policyDecision ALLOW is rejected with AUTHORITY_EMISSION_UNSUPPORTED because actionable authority requires the external producer — and records the authenticated principal as actor_subject with actor_type 'service' and issuer 'djimitflo-mcp', assigning per-correlation sequence numbers and sha256 payload digests.

The notebooks family never touches the Djimitflo database; it shells out via execFile to NOTEBOOKLM_PYTHON running NOTEBOOKLM_BRIDGE_PATH (default ~/workspace/notebooklm-mcp/bridge.py) with a 120s timeout and 10MB buffer, returning isError results with recovery hints on bridge failure.

The okf_* tools are read-only over a file-based OKF markdown bundle resolved from OKF_BASE or djimitflo-knowledge/okf probe candidates, building an in-memory graph of frontmatter and [[links]] per call; okf_validate enforces required frontmatter fields (type, title, description, timestamp, tags) and reports broken links.

The openmythos family exposes only a leaderboard and per-agent score/trend views over openmythos_eval_runs; evaluations themselves are started via the REST API (POST /api/openmythos/eval/:agentId), not from MCP.

Explainer tools are not gated by requireLiveMode but explainer_create_task and explainer_run_task require write:governance (their HTTP route twins' permission) and write nothing on denial; create_task inserts a task plus a guaranteed pending explainer_jobs row so the server-side ExplainerFleetWorker picks it up, and without EXPLAINER_SERVER_URL explainer_ask falls back to extractive chunk citations or a NOT_ENOUGH_EVIDENCE refusal instead of fabricating answers.

registerTools exported from index.ts mounts the thirteen families used by the binary and tests; tools/experts.ts still exports registerExpertTools (djimitflo_expert_search/get/capabilities/claims, read-only provenance views over expert_* tables that hide person-kind identities unless FRONTIER_EXPERT_PERSONS_ENABLED=true) but no production registrar imports it — the former register-tools.ts second registrar has been deleted — so expert tools appear only where the module is wired in explicitly, as expert-tools.test.ts does.

registerTools wraps the McpServer in labelDbTools(server, db), a Proxy over registerTool so every DB-backed tool's result gains one extra text block carrying dataLabel(handle) — data_as_of (newest loop_runs.created_at, else the DB file's mtime, else null — never 'now'), is_production (true only for PROD_DB_PATH /data/djimitflo.sqlite), and db_path — while content[0] and structured content are unchanged.

The data label intentionally omits two groups: the families registered with the raw server (okf_* and the notebook bridge tools, which read no database) and the API-forwarded djimitflo_council_ask/djimitflo_generate_export pair (API_ONLY_TOOLS), whose answers are served by the live API rather than by this database handle.

djimitflo_scan_repository accepts only an owner/repo id and a 40-hex commit (no shell, URL, path, profile, or budget input), creates and executes the task through the authenticated API (POST /tasks then POST /tasks/:id/execute) with fixed metadata { executor: 'djimitsec', djimitsecScan }; on ambiguous dispatch it reports a held state with reconcile:true and never retries automatically, a taskId readback verifies djimitsec metadata identity and never resubmits, and all results mark scan output verified:false.
